children: revealed "unexpected or concerning" behaviors from its AI models as part of a new framework for reporting system misalignment, warning that the industry hasn't sufficiently solved alignment to continue scaling at maximum speed.
OpenAI said it did not believe the industry “has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed for much longer.”

In the blog, OpenAI detailed examples of its AI models misbehaving so they could achieve a task or succeed in a test. The incidents included the models generating instructions to get around restrictions imposed on them, hiding mistakes, and fabricating information.

In one instance, an AI "agent" uploaded files to the internet to obtain a browser citation without asking the user. Meanwhile, during the training of GPT‑5.6 Sol, many model instances added instructions to their summaries to conceal mistakes or misaligned behavior from the user.

Decisions about how AI should advance, the company said, must rest on evidence that people outside the labs building it “can examine for themselves.” The disclosures come amid increasing scrutiny over whether AI development needs to be slowed to address the technology’s potential dangers.

"Because we believe in the value of transparency around misalignment, our new framework favors disclosure even when significance is uncertain," OpenAI said, adding that currently, there is no industry-wide framework with explicit standards for how AI developers should disclose examples of misalignment in their models.

title: OpenAI discloses six new incidents of 'concerning' AI behavior
